title: The Story of the Wind (Valdemar Daa and His Daughters)
summary: "Whew! Hu-u-ush! Let me tell you a story!" howled the Wind as he blew across the ruins of Borreby Castle....
full_text:
"Whew! Hu-u-ush! Let me tell you a story!" howled the Wind as he blew across the ruins of Borreby Castle.

Here lived the proud nobleman Valdemar Daa, who possessed vast forests, fertile fields, and three lovely daughters. But greed devoured his heart. He abandoned his lands to seek the alchemist's philosopher's stone, melting his family silver and mortgaging his estates to feed his fiery crucibles.

The Wind warned him: "Gold is mere dross compared to the gold of loving hearts!"

Valdemar ignored the warning until the castle was seized by creditors. Valdemar and his three daughters walked out as destitute beggars into the cold autumn blast, while the Wind whistled through the empty corridors: "All pride goes down in dust!"
moral: Squandering life and love on the pursuit of gold leaves an empty house in the storm.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Story of the Wind"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
